frontier.hypothesis: Residual A (2 insns) is the last diff in the function: the target emits `subu v1,t5,t1` (dx = x2 - x0) before `subu v0,a2,a3` (az = cz - z0) and we emit az first, while our dz/dx seats are already the target's. Every source rearrangement that fixes the order flips the seats (34 forms measured).
frontier.mechanism: Both subus carry sched1 priority 1 and the same function unit, so rank_for_schedule falls through to the INSN_LUID tie-break and schedule_select's largest-potential-hazard rule (tools/gcc-2.7.2/sched.c:2708-2723); the statement order that lowers dx's LUID also changes local-alloc's quantity numbering, which is what moves dz/dx between $a0 and $v1.
frontier.next_probe: Run tools/ra_solver/inverse_compose.py classify on the dz and dx seats against BOTH 2-floor bodies -- memory/grind/func_8002D780/candidate.c (seats right, order wrong) and tmp/grind/func_8002D780/s5/variantsH/h2_ax_dx_dz_az.c (order right, seats wrong) -- and spell only the C-lever vector it names. In parallel run tools/sched_solver order-exact on the test-3 block: a DEPENDENCE change (not a statement reorder) may break the priority-1 tie the other way without touching allocation, which is the one axis 34 source rearrangements could not reach.

frontier.hypothesis: A decomp-permuter campaign on the 2-floor chassis finds the last 2 insns where the s4 campaign on the 7-floor chassis found nothing.
frontier.mechanism: The s4 campaign's neighbourhood was dominated by two residuals that no local rearrangement could reach; with those closed the remaining residual is a single two-insn local reorder, which is squarely inside the permuter's pass set.
frontier.next_probe: Regenerate base.c from the new candidate.c into the existing validated workspace tmp/grind/func_8002D780/s4/nonmatchings/func_8002D780 (four hurdles + rebuild recipe in evidence.md [s4]), launch with tools/permuter_campaign.py, wait in-turn, harvest with --stop, and re-score every find on the real engine sandbox -- the s4 finding that the permuter's weighted metric is anti-correlated with the engine's here still applies.

frontier.hypothesis: The body is one lever from candidate-ready, so the family classification must be settled before the next submission rather than after a layer-1 verdict.
frontier.mechanism: Review verdicts are keyed by body, so respelling after a layer-1 FAIL is not available; the body carries one FAKE-annotated dead-store re-store and six fresh once-written test-3 difference locals whose named-intermediate-vs-ordinary-C reading the s3 frontier flagged.
frontier.next_probe: Write memory/grind/func_8002D780/self_vet.md now: dead-store family for `m` (quote the scope sentence from .claude/rules/dead-store-fake-exception.md, cite src/code6cac_b.c:1244-1265), and either the six named-intermediate prongs from .claude/rules/narrow-byte-args-packed-call.md plus the 2026-08-17 clarification for ax/az/bx/bz/dz/dx or an ordinary-C argument on the geometry; grep docs/reference/sotn-construct-index.md for vertex-relative difference-local precedent first, and emit a ruling-request rather than a submission if the citation does not hold.
